def: A point-to-point, packet-based serial interconnect between a host's Root Complex and devices, organised as a tree of links. It keeps the PCI software model (configuration space, BARs) but replaces the shared parallel bus.
The component at the root of a PCIe hierarchy that connects the CPU and memory subsystem to PCIe: it turns CPU accesses into PCIe requests, device DMA into memory accesses, and hosts Root Ports.
A downstream port of the Root Complex that heads one PCIe link and the hierarchy below it; software sees it as a PCI-to-PCI bridge (Type 1 header).

A component that fans one upstream link out to several downstream links, appearing to software as an upstream bridge, an internal bus and one bridge per downstream port. It routes TLPs by address or ID.
A PCIe function that requests or completes transactions on its own behalf (Type 0 configuration header), such as an NVMe SSD controller.
An endpoint built into the Root Complex itself, with no PCIe link of its own.
The PCI address of a function (for example 01:00.0), assigned during enumeration; also forms the Requester ID used to route completions. The bus number is logical, not a shared wire.
The smallest unit of a PCIe link: one transmit differential pair and one receive differential pair (four wires), carrying serial data in both directions simultaneously.
One or more lanes between exactly two PCIe ports, operating together with packets striped across all lanes. Width and speed are negotiated during training.
The number of lanes in a link (x1, x2, x4, x8, x16). The maximum is a capability; the negotiated width is reported in Link Status.
Shorthand for a per-lane signalling rate: Gen1 2.5, Gen2 5.0, Gen3 8.0, Gen4 16.0, Gen5 32.0, Gen6 64.0, Gen7 128.0 GT/s. Independent of the NVMe specification revision.
Symbols transferred per second per lane per direction, before encoding overhead. For NRZ rates one transfer is one bit; for PAM4 rates the quoted GT/s is the per-lane bit rate.
Two conductors carrying complementary signals; the receiver measures their difference, rejecting common-mode noise and reducing emissions.
A series capacitor on each leg of a PCIe transmit pair that blocks DC between ports; it also shapes the receiver-detection measurement.
Receiver circuitry that derives sampling timing from transitions in the incoming data, so PCIe needs no per-lane clock wire.
The 100 MHz reference from which PCIe ports generate their transmit rate; supplied in common-clock, SRNS or SRIS architectures.
Sideband signal that holds a device in fundamental reset until power and REFCLK are stable; its de-assertion starts link training.
A protocol-aware device in a PCIe channel that recovers and retransmits the signal with fresh timing and participates in link training and equalisation; invisible to configuration software.
A protocol-unaware analog amplifier/equaliser in a channel; boosts signal (and noise) without re-timing it.
Handling, during Configuration, of a board where lane order is mirrored between the two ports, so the link still forms with correct logical lane numbers.
Automatic correction, during Polling, of a differential pair whose positive and negative legs are swapped; receivers are required to support it.
Encoding used at 2.5 and 5.0 GT/s that maps each byte to a 10-bit symbol for DC balance, transitions and control symbols; costs 20 % of the raw rate.
Encoding used at 8.0, 16.0 and 32.0 GT/s (non-flit): 128-bit blocks with a 2-bit sync header plus scrambling; overhead about 1.5 %.
Two-level signalling carrying one bit per unit interval; used by PCIe up to 32 GT/s.
Four-level signalling carrying two bits per symbol; used at 64 and 128 GT/s so the symbol rate stays half the bit rate, at the cost of smaller eyes and a need for FEC.
PCIe 6.0+ mode that carries traffic in fixed 256-byte flits (236 TLP bytes, 6 Data Link payload bytes, 8 CRC bytes, 6 FEC bytes); required at 64 GT/s and above.
Redundant information added so the receiver can correct errors without retransmission; lightweight FEC protects Flit Mode flits at PAM4 rates.
The PCIe packet that carries a request, completion or message between requester and completer, routed hop by hop across links.
A small link-local packet (Ack, Nak, flow-control InitFC/UpdateFC, power management) generated and consumed by the Data Link Layers of the two ports on one link.
32-bit CRC added by the Data Link Layer to each TLP (with its sequence number) in non-flit mode and checked by the receiving port on the same link.
The Data Link Layer's retransmission scheme: receivers acknowledge good TLPs by sequence number (Ack) or request replay (Nak); transmitters replay from a retry buffer.
Transmitter memory holding every TLP sent but not yet acknowledged, so it can be retransmitted after a Nak or replay-timer timeout.
PCIe's credit-based mechanism: a transmitter may send a TLP only if the receiver has advertised enough header and data credits (data credit = 16 bytes) for that type (Posted, Non-Posted, Completion).
A Physical Layer sequence sent on all lanes simultaneously for link management: TS1, TS2, SKP, EIOS, EIEOS, FTS, SDS.
Training ordered set carrying link/lane numbers, N_FTS, supported data rates, training control and equalisation fields; generally used to propose.
Training ordered set with the same layout as TS1, generally used to confirm agreement and move to the next training step.
Ordered set inserted periodically so receivers can compensate clock-frequency differences in their elastic buffers.
Sent before a transmitter enters electrical idle (low-power states, speed changes).
Sent when leaving electrical idle at 8 GT/s and above and periodically during training; also aids block alignment.
Ordered set used to re-lock a receiver quickly when leaving L0s; the receiver's needed count is N_FTS.
Ordered set marking the start of a data stream after ordered sets at 128b/130b rates.

exp: Link Training and Status State Machine
def: The Physical Layer state machine in each port (Detect, Polling, Configuration, L0, Recovery, L0s, L1, L2, Hot Reset, Disabled, Loopback) that trains, operates, recovers and power-manages a link.
Detect-state test in which a transmitter senses whether a terminated receiver is present on each lane, by the time its line voltage takes to follow a common-mode step.
Per-rate negotiated tuning of transmitter FIR settings (presets/coefficients) and receiver adaptation at 8 GT/s and above, performed in Recovery in Phases 0–3.
Hardware-autonomous entry into link low-power states (L0s, L1) while the device stays in D0, enabled through Link Control.
A device reading or writing host memory itself, using PCIe memory requests, without the CPU copying the data.
Light per-direction link power state entered by an idle transmitter and exited with FTS; not used in Flit Mode.
Link power state with both directions idle, entered by handshake (ASPM or software PM), exited through Recovery; may have substates L1.1 and L1.2.
Flit Mode power state in which a link reduces its active width while remaining in L0.
Platform configuration that splits one group of Root Port lanes (for example x16) into several narrower ports (for example 4 × x4).
PCIe 4.0+ capability letting software step a receiver's sampling point in time and voltage to measure per-lane margin in-system.
